It comprehensively amends multiple titles of the U.S. Code to streamline definitions such as contingency operations and reserve component duty, affecting all members of the reserve components and National Guard, and aligns benefits across federal programs.

card.summary: H.R. 6976, titled the Duty Status Reform Act, amends and reorganizes federal laws relating to duty performed by members of the reserve components of the Armed Forces, including the National Guard and the Coast Guard Reserve. The bill consolidates various authorities used to order reserve component members to perform duty into distinct categories, aligns benefits and survivor benefits across different duty statuses, repeals several older statutory sections, and updates numerous cross-references in federal law.
card.title: Duty Status Reform Act

summary: The Duty Status Reform Act simplifies and consolidates the various legal authorities and categories under which members of the reserve components of the Armed Forces and the National Guard can be ordered to perform duty. It reorganizes these authorities into four distinct categories: active duty, reserve component duty, remote assignments, and specific purposes, while aligning benefits, survivor benefits, and National Guard provisions across federal law.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to consolidated duty authorities, standardized definitions, and aligned pay, benefits, and retirement point calculations.

affected_groups.group: National Guard Members (Army National Guard and Air National Guard)

key_provisions: Consolidates authorities to order reserve component members to perform duty into a structured chapter dividing duty into active duty, reserve component duty, and remote assignments.
Renames and standardizes terminology such as replacing inactive-duty training with reserve component duty across multiple titles of the U.S. Code.
Updates provisions regarding the National Guard in title 32, including training, duty authorities, the National Guard Youth Challenge Program, and boundary restrictions.
Aligns federal benefits, survivor benefits, and administrative requirements for reserve component and National Guard members with those of active-duty personnel.
Provides transition rules, including early access to TRICARE up to 180 days before certain active duty or full-time National Guard duty orders commence.
Establishes a general effective date 10 years after enactment, with a process for an earlier effective date through joint agency certifications and subsequent legislation.

summary_detail.significance: The bill reorganizes decades of complex and fragmented statutes governing reserve component and National Guard duty into a unified framework. By consolidating numerous authorities and standardizing definitions, pay, and benefits across titles 5, 10, 14, 32, 37, and 38, the legislation impacts administrative procedures and benefits management for the entire reserve force.
